theory: The supplied booklet teaches reverse-chain integration for linear inner functions only (lines 325–449); the intro, nonlinear examples, facts and steps extend the method beyond that teaching. Restrict the teaching and dependent items to the supported linear-power method, state $a\ne0$ and $n\ne-1$, and require continuity on the integration interval when using endpoint evaluation. The statement 'A constant multiple of $f'(x)$ is enough: divide by that constant at the end' reverses the adjustment: an outside factor $k f'(x)$ requires multiplication by $k$; division applies when compensating for an inserted inner-derivative coefficient.
summary: Restricted the theory to linear-power primitives, corrected constant-factor adjustment, and stated the parameter and continuity requirements.
